claim: PRDM13 is a transcriptional repressor present in progenitor domains of the dorsal but not the ventral neural tube from hindbrain regions to the spinal cord.
source: PRDM13 is a transcriptional repressor present in progenitor domains of the dorsal but not the ventral neural tube from hindbrain regions to the spinal cord (Chang et al., 2013) (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chang et al., 2013 and reference to Figure 1C showing expression pattern.

claim: PRDM13 is a member of the PRDM family of proteins defined by an N-terminal PR domain and a varying number of C-terminal zinc-finger (ZF) domains.
source: It is a member of the PRDM family of proteins defined by an N-terminal PR domain and a varying number of C-terminal zinc-finger (ZF) domains (Hohenauer and Moore, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hohenauer and Moore, 2012 describing PRDM family characteristics.

claim: PRDM factors function in a variety of cell lineages to promote cell proliferation and cell type specification.
source: PRDM factors function in a variety of cell lineages to promote cell proliferation and cell type specification (Bikoff et al., 2009; Eom et al., 2009; Huang et al., 1998; Ross et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations describing PRDM factor functions.

claim: PRDM13 functions as a downstream effector of PTF1A to suppress the excitatory neuronal program within the inhibitory neuronal lineage in the dorsal spinal cord.
source: Within the dorsal spinal cord, PRDM13 functions as a downstream effector of PTF1A to suppress the excitatory neuronal program within the inhibitory neuronal lineage.
evidence: Stated as a known function in the introduction, supported by subsequent experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Several PRDM family members have intrinsic histone methyltransferase activity mediated by the PR domain.
source: Several PRDM family members have been shown to have intrinsic histone methyltransferase activity mediated by the PR domain (Di Zazzo et al., 2013; Fog et al., 2012; Fumasoni et al., 2007; Hohenauer and Moore, 2012).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations describing histone methyltransferase activity of PRDM family members.

claim: PRDM13 has been suggested to have intrinsic histone methyltransferase activity, although the relevance of this in vivo remains unclear.
source: PRDM13 has been suggested to have intrinsic histone methyltransferase activity, although the relevance of this in vivo remains unclear (Hanotel et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by citation to Hanotel et al., 2014, with acknowledgment of uncertainty about in vivo relevance.

claim: The overexpressed PRDM13 ZF domain is sufficient to specify inhibitory neurons in retina and neural tube.
source: since the overexpressed PRDM13 ZF domain is sufficient to specify inhibitory neurons in retina and neural tube (Chang et al., 2013; Watanabe et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chang et al., 2013 and Watanabe et al., 2015 describing overexpression experiments.

claim: Prdm13GFP and Prdm13ΔZF mutant mice are neonatal lethal.
source: Heterozygous animals are indistinguishable from wild-type littermates, but when homozygous for the mutant allele they die at birth, similar to the neonatal lethality seen in other mutants null for TFs that regulate neuronal differentiation and specification such as the bHLH factors ASCL1 and PTF1A (Glasgow et al., 2005; Guillemot and Joyner, 1993).
evidence: Directly stated observation from the mutant mice generated in this study, with comparison to other mutants.

claim: PRDM13-specific antibodies do not detect protein in Prdm13GFP and Prdm13ΔZF mutants at E11.5 by Western blot or immunofluorescence.
source: PRDM13-specific antibodies generated to the C-terminal domain (Watanabe et al., 2015) do not detect protein in these mutants at E11.5 by Western blot or immunofluorescence (Figure 1F–H,J).
evidence: Supported by Western blot and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1F-H,J.

claim: Prdm13∆115/∆115 mutant mice survive into adulthood.
source: Surprisingly, Prdm13∆115/∆115 survives into adulthood, similar to a previously reported Prdm13 mutant that deleted exons 2 and 3 that encodes much of the PR domain of the protein (Watanabe et al., 2015).
evidence: Direct observation from the mutant mice generated in this study, with comparison to previously reported mutant.

claim: Western analysis and immunohistochemistry reveal that a protein containing at least the C-terminal ZF domain is translated in Prdm13∆115 mutants.
source: Western analysis and immunohistochemistry reveal that a protein containing at least the C-terminal ZF domain is translated in Prdm13∆115 (Figure 1I,J).
evidence: Supported by Western blot and immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1I,J.

claim: Prdm13GFP and Prdm13ΔZF mutant embryos show loss of PAX2+;LHX1/5+ dI4 neurons in the dorsal neural tube at E10.5.
source: A complete loss of dI4 (PAX2+;LHX1/5+) and an increase in dI3/5 (TLX1/3+) in both the Prdm13GFP/GFP and Prdm13ΔZF/ΔZF neural tubes was seen at this stage.
evidence: Directly stated observation supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2.

claim: Prdm13GFP and Prdm13ΔZF mutant embryos show an increase in TLX1/3+ dI3/5 neurons in the dorsal neural tube at E10.5.
source: A complete loss of dI4 (PAX2+;LHX1/5+) and an increase in dI3/5 (TLX1/3+) in both the Prdm13GFP/GFP and Prdm13ΔZF/ΔZF neural tubes was seen at this stage.
evidence: Directly stated observation supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2.

claim: The phenotypes of Prdm13GFP and Prdm13ΔZF mutants are identical to the Ptf1a null mouse at E10.5.
source: These phenotypes are identical to the Ptf1a null mouse (Figure 2G) (Glasgow et al., 2005)
evidence: Comparison stated in text and supported by quantification in Figure 2G and citation to Glasgow et al., 2005.

claim: PRDM13 functions as a repressor of the excitatory neuronal gene program within the inhibitory neuronal lineage in the dorsal neural tube.
source: Thus, these findings confirm PRDM13 functions as a repressor of the excitatory neuronal gene program within the inhibitory neuronal lineage in the dorsal neural tube.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing loss of PAX2+ cells and increase in TLX1/3+ cells in mutants.

claim: Prdm13 mutants show a marked reduction of the dI2 population (LHX1/5+; PAX2-) that is not seen with the loss of Ptf1a.
source: One important distinction is the marked reduction of the dI2 population (LHX1/5+; PAX2-) in the Prdm13 mutants that is not seen with the loss of Ptf1a (Figure 2).
evidence: Directly stated observation supported by quantification in Figure 2G.

claim: Both Prdm13GFP/GFP and Prdm13ΔZF/ΔZF neural tubes show only partial loss of PAX2+ cells dorsally at E12.5 and E16.5.
source: Both Prdm13GFP/GFP and Prdm13ΔZF/ΔZF neural tubes show only partial loss of PAX2+ cells dorsally at E12.5 and E16.5, markedly different from the absolute loss of PAX2 observed in the Ptf1aCRE/CRE null (Figure 3A–G)
evidence: Directly stated observation supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 3A-G.

claim: The partial loss of PAX2+ cells in Prdm13 mutants is accompanied by a modest increase in the number of TLX1/3+ cells.
source: This partial loss of PAX2+ cells was accompanied by a modest increase in the number of TLX1/3+ cells in the Prdm13 mutants, which was not as dramatic as the increase seen in the Ptf1a null (Figure 3H).
evidence: Directly stated observation supported by quantification in Figure 3H.

claim: Gad1 is only partially lost dorsally in Prdm13 mutants at E16.5, in contrast to the complete loss in Ptf1a null animals.
source: Consistent with only a partial loss of PAX2+ cells in the Prdm13 mutants, Gad1, required for synthesis of the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA, is also only partially lost dorsally as seen by in situ hybridization at E16.5 (Figure 3I–K). Again this contrasts to the complete loss of this marker in the Ptf1a null animals at these later stages (Glasgow et al., 2005).
evidence: Directly stated observation supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 3I-K and citation to Glasgow et al., 2005.

claim: Only a modest increase in Vglut2 (Slc17a6) is detected in the lateral region of the domain lacking Gad1 in Prdm13 mutants.
source: Similarly, only a modest increase in Vglut2 (Slc17a6), a marker of excitatory neurons, is detected in the lateral region of the domain lacking Gad1 (Figure 3L–N).
evidence: Directly stated observation supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 3L-N.

claim: 837 genes had greater than a 1.5-fold difference in expression and an FPKM >1 in at least one of the conditions in RNA-seq comparing Prdm13GFP/+ versus Prdm13GFP/GFP neural tubes.
source: 837 genes had greater than a 1.5-fold difference in expression and an FPKM >1 in at least one of the conditions.
evidence: Directly stated result from RNA-seq analysis.

claim: A large number of the differentially expressed genes in the Prdm13 mutants play a role in cell proliferation, neuronal specification and cell cycle regulation.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis determined that a large number of the DEGs in the Prdm13 mutants play a role in cell proliferation, neuronal specification and cell cycle regulation (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Result from GO analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: 220 PRDM13 binding sites were identified by ChIP-seq, largely located at distal sites relative to the transcription start sites of genes.
source: We identified 220 PRDM13 binding sites largely located at distal sites relative to the transcription start sites of genes.
evidence: Directly stated result from ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: PRDM13 binds to a region >20 kb 5' of Tlx3 that was previously shown to be a Tlx3 enhancer.
source: The genome tracks for the Tlx3 locus showing RNA-Seq and ChIP-Seq data illustrate the increase in Tlx3 transcripts in the dorsal neural tube of Prdm13 mutants relative to wild type, and the binding of PRDM13 to a region >20 kb 5' of Tlx3 (Figure 4B). This region was previously shown to drive expression of a reporter gene to the dI3/dI5 domains in the chick neural tube, identifying it as a Tlx3 enhancer (Chang et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq data in Figure 4B and citation to Chang et al., 2013.

claim: The primary motif in PRDM13 bound regions is an E-box (bHLH binding motif) found in 40% of the sites.
source: De novo motif analysis failed to identify a novel binding motif unique to PRDM13, but PRDM13 bound sites were enriched for motifs for known neural TFs such as E-box (bHLH) (40%), Rfx (17%), Pdx (HD) (25%) and Sox (30%) motifs (Figure 4C).
evidence: Result from de novo motif analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Almost half of the PRDM13 bound sites overlap with the E-box binding factors ASCL1, PTF1A, or both.
source: Indeed, almost half of the PRDM13 bound sites overlap with the E-box binding factors ASCL1 (15), PTF1A (48), or both (39) (Figure 4D).
evidence: Result from comparison of ChIP-seq datasets shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The lack of a unique binding motif for PRDM13 is consistent with a model where PRDM13 is recruited to sites by other site-specific TFs.
source: The lack of a unique binding motif is consistent with a model where PRDM13 is recruited to sites by other site-specific TFs.
evidence: Inference drawn from the motif analysis results.

claim: 60 putative direct targets of PRDM13 were identified by intersecting genes associated with PRDM13 ChIP-seq peaks with differentially expressed genes in Prdm13 mutants.
source: 60 putative direct targets of PRDM13 were identified by intersecting these genes with the DEGs identified in Prdm13GFP neural tubes (Figure 4A, Supplemental file 3).
evidence: Result from intersection of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq datasets shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 54 of the putative PRDM13 targets have increased mRNA levels in Prdm13 mutants relative to controls (p-value=1.26e-27).
source: Consistent with the reported function of PRDM13 as a transcriptional repressor (Chang et al., 2013), mRNA levels for 54 of the putative targets are increased in Prdm13 mutants relative to controls (p-value=1.26e-27) whereas only six are decreased (p-value=0.16) (Figure 4A).
evidence: Statistical analysis of RNA-seq data for genes with PRDM13 binding, shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Tlx3 is elevated 17-fold in the absence of Prdm13.
source: Consistently, Tlx3 is elevated 17-fold, while Pax2 is reduced 6.3-fold in the absence of Prdm13 (Table 1).
evidence: Result from RNA-seq analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: Pax2 is reduced 6.3-fold in the absence of Prdm13.
source: Consistently, Tlx3 is elevated 17-fold, while Pax2 is reduced 6.3-fold in the absence of Prdm13 (Table 1).
evidence: Result from RNA-seq analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: Ptf1a was upregulated 3.5-fold by RNA-seq in the Prdm13 mutants relative to control.
source: Ptf1a was upregulated 3.5-fold by RNA-seq in the Prdm13 mutants relative to control (Table 1).
evidence: Result from RNA-seq analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: The increase in PTF1A in Prdm13 mutants is localized within its normal dorsal progenitor domain 4 (dP4).
source: The increase in PTF1A is localized within its normal dorsal progenitor domain 4 (dP4) (Figure 5A–F).
evidence: Observation from in situ hybridization and immunofluorescence shown in Figure 5A-F.

claim: There is a negative feedback loop between PRDM13 and PTF1A where PRDM13 feeds back to repress transcription of Ptf1a.
source: Because PTF1A is a transcriptional activator of Prdm13 transcription (Chang et al., 2013) these data reveal a negative feedback loop between PRDM13 and PTF1A (Figure 5G) where the product of the activated gene (PRDM13) feeds back to repress transcription of its activator (Ptf1a) (Alon, 2007).
evidence: Inference from the observation that Ptf1a is upregulated in Prdm13 mutants, combined with known activation of Prdm13 by PTF1A.

claim: PRDM13 is bound to the Ptf1a autoregulatory enhancer region by ChIP-seq.
source: Indeed, ChIP-seq experiments demonstrate PRDM13 is bound to this enhancer region (Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Result from ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: PRDM13 overexpression blocks GFP reporter activity driven by the 2.3 kb Ptf1a autoregulatory enhancer in chick electroporation assays.
source: In contrast, co-electroporation with a Prdm13 expression vector alone or along with that for Ptf1a blocks reporter activity completely (Figure 5K–M).
evidence: Result from chick electroporation reporter assays shown in Figure 5K-M.

claim: PRDM13 and PTF1A interact as shown by co-IP assays.
source: Finally, we show that PRDM13 and PTF1A interact, possibly forming a repressor complex, using co-IP assays with lysates from HEK293 cells transfected with FLAG-PRDM13 and MYC-PTF1A (Figure 5N).
evidence: Result from co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 5N.

claim: PRDM13 interacts with ASCL1 by co-IP.
source: Because PRDM13 also interacts by co-IP with ASCL1 (Chang et al., 2013) (Figure 5O)
evidence: Result from co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 5O and cited from Chang et al., 2013.

claim: PRDM13 does not interact with E-proteins E47, E12, and HEB by co-IP.
source: We detected no interaction between PRDM13 and the E-proteins E47 and E12 (2 isoforms of Tcf3), and HEB (Tcf12) (Figure 5O).
evidence: Result from co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 5O.

claim: Olig1 and Olig2 show ectopic dorsal expression in Prdm13GFP/GFP neural tubes (217-fold and 1114-fold increase, respectively).
source: Upon loss of PRDM13, the linked genes Olig1 and Olig2 show striking ectopic dorsal expression within Prdm13GFP/GFP neural tubes (Table 1, 217-fold and 1114-fold, respectively).
evidence: Result from RNA-seq analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: The ectopic OLIG2 in Prdm13 mutants is localized just lateral to the progenitor domain in the dorsal neural tube.
source: The ectopic OLIG2 is localized just lateral to the progenitor domain in the dorsal neural tube (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: Observation from immunofluorescence shown in Figure 6A-C.

claim: Aberrant expression of OLIG2 is not detected in the Ptf1a null even though there is a partial loss of PRDM13 in these mutants.
source: This aberrant expression of OLIG2 is not detected in the Ptf1a null even though there is a partial loss of PRDM13 in these mutants (Figure 6D).
evidence: Observation from immunofluorescence shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The ectopic OLIG2 in Prdm13 mutants is restricted to the dI4 domain and co-expresses with TLX1/3 and PTF1A.
source: Co-labeling of OLIG2 with TLX1/3, PTF1A, and OLIG3 demonstrate the ectopic OLIG2 is restricted to the dI4 domain (Figure 6E–H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1). Notably, the ectopic OLIG2 expressing cells co-express TLX1/3 and PTF1A (Figure 6E–H), factors that are never co-expressed during normal development, thus indicating a severe disruption of neuronal subtype identity in the dorsal neural tube.
evidence: Observation from immunofluorescence shown in Figure 6E-H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: PRDM13 ChIP-seq identified three genomic regions (e1Olig, e2Olig, e3Olig) surrounding the Olig genes bound by PRDM13.
source: To explore whether a similar mechanism is involved in regulating the linked genes Olig1 and Olig2, we identified three genomic regions surrounding the Olig genes bound by PRDM13 from ChIP-seq (Figure 6I and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Result from ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 6I and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: All three PRDM13 bound sites near Olig genes (e1Olig, e2Olig, e3Olig) are also bound by PTF1A and/or ASCL1.
source: All three of these sites, designated as e1Olig, e2Olig and e3Olig, are also bound by PTF1A and/or ASCL1.
evidence: Result from comparison of ChIP-seq datasets.

claim: Only e2Olig contains the compound E-box/TC-box motifs that represent the site bound by the PTF1 trimeric complex.
source: Of these three sites, only e2Olig contains the compound E-box/TC-box motifs that represent the site bound by the PTF1 trimeric complex (Figure 6J).
evidence: Result from sequence analysis shown in Figure 6J.

claim: All three regions (e1Olig, e2Olig, e3Olig) directed expression of GFP in the neural tube, and this activity was suppressed by PRDM13.
source: All three regions directed expression of GFP in the neural tube, activity that was suppressed by PRDM13 (Figure 6K–l,O,U,V and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Result from chick electroporation reporter assays shown in Figure 6K-l,O,U,V and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: e2Olig::GFP but not e1Olig::GFP or e3Olig::GFP was activated by PTF1A in chick electroporation assays.
source: We tested whether PTF1A or ASCL1 were sufficient to activate the Olig enhancers by co-electroporating them individually with each enhancer-reporter. e2Olig::GFP but not e1Olig::GFP or e3Olig::GFP was activated by PTF1A, and this activity was suppressed by PRDM13 (Figure 6M–O and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E,J).
evidence: Result from chick electroporation reporter assays shown in Figure 6M-O and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E,J.

claim: ASCL1 did not increase activity through the Olig enhancers in chick electroporation assays.
source: ASCL1 did not increase activity through these enhancers.
evidence: Result from chick electroporation reporter assays.

claim: e2Olig::GFP enhancer activity and its induction by PTF1A is lost when E-boxes that conform to a PTF1 motif are mutated.
source: Indeed, e2Olig::GFP enhancer activity and its induction by PTF1A is lost when E-boxes that conform to a PTF1 motif are mutated (Figure 6P,R).
evidence: Result from chick electroporation reporter assays with mutated enhancers shown in Figure 6P,R.

claim: Prdm12 mRNA is strikingly upregulated in the Prdm13GFP/GFP mutants (24-fold increase).
source: Like Olig1 and Olig2, Prdm12 mRNA is strikingly upregulated in the Prdm13GFP/GFP mutants (Table 1, 24-fold).
evidence: Result from RNA-seq analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: Ectopic Prdm12 expression is verified in Prdm13GFP/GFP and Prdm13ΔZF/ΔZF neural tubes by mRNA in situ hybridization.
source: We verified the ectopic Prdm12 expression in Prdm13GFP/GFP and Prdm13ΔZF/ΔZF neural tubes by mRNA in situ hybridization (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: Result from in situ hybridization shown in Figure 7A-C.

claim: Misregulation of Prdm12 is not detected in Ptf1a mutants.
source: This misregulation of Prdm12 is not detected in Ptf1a mutants (Figure 7D).
evidence: Observation from in situ hybridization shown in Figure 7D.

claim: PRDM13 ChIP-seq identified a site (e1Prdm12) overlapping a binding site for PTF1A near the Prdm12 gene.
source: To determine if PRDM13 and PTF1A are directly regulating Prdm12, we analyzed the Prdm12 genomic region for sites bound by these factors. PRDM13 ChIP-seq identified a site, e1Prdm12, overlapping a binding site for PTF1A (Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Result from ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: e1Prdm12 contains an E-box, but no compound E-box/TC-box for the PTF1 trimer complex binding.
source: e1Prdm12 contains an E-box, but no compound E-box/TC-box for the PTF1 trimer complex binding (Figure 7F).
evidence: Result from sequence analysis shown in Figure 7F.

claim: e1Prdm12::GFP directs reporter expression localized to the endogenous Prdm12 domain and is repressed by PRDM13.
source: e1Prdm12::GFP directs reporter expression localized to the endogenous Prdm12 domain and is repressed by PRDM13 (Figure 7G,H,J).
evidence: Result from chick electroporation reporter assays shown in Figure 7G,H,J.

claim: Co-electroporation with Ptf1a had no effect on e1Prdm12::GFP reporter activity.
source: However, co-electroporation with Ptf1a had no effect (Figure 7I,J).
evidence: Result from chick electroporation reporter assays shown in Figure 7I,J.

claim: Both Neurog1 and Neurog2 are increased in Prdm13GFP/GFP mutants (3.4- and 1.7-fold respectively).
source: Support for these bHLH factors being involved in the ectopic dorsal expression of Prdm12 was suggested by the RNA-seq data that showed both Neurog1 and Neurog2 as being increased in Prdm13GFP/GFP mutants (Table 1, 3.4- and 1.7-fold respectively).
evidence: Result from RNA-seq analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: mRNA in situ hybridization shows both Neurog1 and Neurog2 increased in the dorsal neural tube of the Prdm13 mutants.
source: Indeed, mRNA in situ hybridization shows both of these factors increased in the dorsal neural tube of the Prdm13 mutants (Figure 7L,N).
evidence: Result from in situ hybridization shown in Figure 7L,N.

claim: Both NEUROG1 and NEUROG2 drive activity of the e1Prdm12::GFP reporter, and this activity is suppressed when Prdm13 is added.
source: We co-electroporated expression constructs for Neurog1 and Neurog2 with the Prdm12 enhancer reporter e1Prdm12::GFP and found that both drive activity of the reporter, activity that is suppressed when Prdm13 is added (Figure 7O–S).
evidence: Result from chick electroporation reporter assays shown in Figure 7O-S.

claim: PRDM13 interacts with NEUROG1 and NEUROG2 using co-IP assays.
source: And finally, we show that PRDM13 interacts with NEUROG1 and NEUROG2 using co-IP assays with lysates from HEK293 cells transfected with these factors (Figure 7T).
evidence: Result from co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 7T.

claim: The C-terminal ZF domain of PRDM13 is required for PRDM13 function in neuronal specification in the neural tube and survival of the animals.
source: The Prdm13 mutants generated here, particularly the Prdm13ΔZF mutants, highlight the requirement for the C-terminal ZF domain for PRDM13 function in neuronal specification in the neural tube and survival of the animals.
evidence: Inference from the phenotypes of different mutant alleles, particularly the lethality of Prdm13ΔZF mutants.

claim: The Prdm13Δ115 and Prdm13Δ2/3 mutants are hypomorphic alleles.
source: We postulate that the Prdm13Δ2/3 and Prdm13Δ115 are hypomorphic alleles, and that the ZF domain encoded within exon four is produced in tissues that support survival.
evidence: Speculation based on the survival of these mutants and detection of protein containing the ZF domain.

claim: PTF1A directly induces transcription of Prdm13 in mice, chicken, and Xenopus.
source: PTF1A, essential for specification inhibitory neurons in various regions of the nervous system, directly induces transcription of Prdm13 in mice, chicken, and Xenopus (Chang et al., 2013; Hanotel et al., 2014; Meredith et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chang et al., 2013; Hanotel et al., 2014; Meredith et al., 2013.

claim: PRDM13 feedback inhibits its own expression as reported in Xenopus and detected in mouse mutants.
source: PRDM13 in turn feedback inhibits its own expression as reported in Xenopus (Hanotel et al., 2014) and detected here in the mouse mutants (Table 1)
evidence: Supported by citation to Hanotel et al., 2014 and RNA-seq data in Table 1.

claim: The inhibition of Ptf1a by PRDM13 represents an incoherent feedback loop.
source: The inhibition of Ptf1a by PRDM13 represents an incoherent feedback loop, a mechanism present in multiple TF networks (Alon, 2007).
evidence: Classification of the regulatory mechanism with citation to Alon, 2007.

claim: PRDM13 is localized to the same sites in vivo as seen by ChIP-Seq from neural tubes as neural bHLH factors like ASCL1 and PTF1A.
source: (1) PRDM13 and neural bHLH factors like ASCL1 and PTF1A are localized to the same sites in vivo as seen by ChIP-Seq from neural tubes.
evidence: Result from ChIP-seq analysis comparing PRDM13, ASCL1, and PTF1A binding sites.

claim: PRDM13 and multiple class II bHLH factors, but not class I bHLH factors, co-immunoprecipitate.
source: (2) PRDM13 and multiple class II bHLH factors, but not class I bHLH factors, co-immunoprecipitate.
evidence: Result from co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Neural bHLH factors activate transcription through identified regulatory regions in reporter assays while PRDM13 blocks this activity.
source: (3) Neural bHLH factors activate transcription through the identified regulatory regions in reporter assays while PRDM13 blocks this activity.
evidence: Result from chick electroporation reporter assays.

claim: Loss of PRDM13 function in vivo results in ectopic expression of multiple bHLH regulated genes in the dorsal neural tube.
source: (4) Loss of PRDM13 function in vivo results in ectopic expression of multiple bHLH regulated genes in the dorsal neural tube.
evidence: Result from RNA-seq and in situ hybridization in Prdm13 mutants.

claim: The primary binding motif identified by PRDM13 ChIP-Seq is an E-box, the motif for bHLH factors.
source: (5) The primary binding motif identified by PRDM13 ChIP-Seq is an E-box, the motif for bHLH factors.
evidence: Result from de novo motif analysis of PRDM13 ChIP-seq data.

claim: PRDM8 and BHLHB5 form a transcription repressor complex where BHLHB5 is the specific DNA binding factor that recruits PRDM8.
source: Ross et al. propose PRDM8 and BHLHB5 form a transcription repressor complex where BHLHB5 is the specific DNA binding factor that recruits PRDM8.
evidence: Cited model from Ross et al., 2012.

claim: PRDM8 does not bind DNA targets in the absence of BHLHB5.
source: In support of this model, PRDM8 does not bind DNA targets in the absence of BHLHB5 (Ross et al., 2012).
evidence: Cited finding from Ross et al., 2012.

claim: PRDM13 is required to restrict expression of multiple neuronal specification factors to the ventral neural tube to ensure precision in cell-fate identity in the dorsal spinal cord.
source: Finally, this study demonstrates PRDM13 is required to restrict expression of multiple neuronal specification factors to the ventral neural tube to ensure precision in cell-fate identity in the dorsal spinal cord (Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Summary conclusion from the study supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: NKX2.2, NKX6.1 and OLIG2 directly repress all alternative fates, including dorsal cell fate programs, in the ventral neural tube.
source: However, two recent studies of the ventral neural tube TFs NKX2.2, NKX6.1 and OLIG2 uncover broader programs of repression than previously appreciated and demonstrate that these transcription factors directly repress all alternative fates, including dorsal cell fate programs, in the ventral neural tube (Kutejova et al., 2016; Nishi et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited findings from Kutejova et al., 2016 and Nishi et al., 2015.

claim: PRDM13 is a key transcriptional repressor of a whole battery of genes, including factors normally restricted to the ventral neural tube and required for neuronal identity in that region.
source: Here we provide evidence for an additional variation of these models whereby the transcriptional repressor is broadly expressed and it limits inappropriate gene expression driven by progenitor-specific activators, the bHLH factors. PRDM13 is identified as a key transcriptional repressor of a whole battery of genes, not just those in domains adjacent to the domain giving rise to the dorsal inhibitory neurons, but also factors normally restricted to the ventral neural tube and required for neuronal identity in that region (Table 1) (Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Summary conclusion from the study supported by RNA-seq data in Table 1 and Figure 8.

claim: OLIG2 and PRDM12 are normally restricted to the ventral neural tube but in the Prdm13 mutants they are aberrantly present dorsally, altering the identity of these neurons.
source: In particular, we highlight OLIG2 and PRDM12, which are normally restricted to the ventral neural tube but in the Prdm13 mutants they are aberrantly present dorsally, altering the identity of these neurons.
evidence: Summary of findings from immunofluorescence and in situ hybridization data.

claim: PRDM13 is a transcriptional repressor essential in the dorsal spinal cord development to modulate the transcriptional activity of neural bHLH factors to generate precise neuronal identities.
source: Taken together, PRDM13 is a transcriptional repressor essential in the dorsal spinal cord development to modulate the transcriptional activity of neural bHLH factors to generate precise neuronal identities.
evidence: Summary conclusion from the entire study.

claim: PRDM13 inhibits gene expression programs for excitatory neuronal lineages in the dorsal neural tube.
source: PRDM13 inhibits gene expression programs for excitatory neuronal lineages in the dorsal neural tube.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by data showing increased TLX1/3 in mutants.

claim: PRDM13 ensures a battery of ventral neural tube specification genes such as Olig1, Olig2 and Prdm12 are excluded dorsally.
source: Strikingly, PRDM13 also ensures a battery of ventral neural tube specification genes such as Olig1, Olig2 and Prdm12 are excluded dorsally.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by RNA-seq and in situ hybridization data.

claim: PRDM13 restricts gene expression in specific neuronal lineages via recruitment to chromatin by multiple neural bHLH factors.
source: PRDM13 does this via recruitment to chromatin by multiple neural bHLH factors to restrict gene expression in specific neuronal lineages.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data showing overlap with bHLH binding sites and co-IP data.

claim: ASCL1 induces the excitatory neuron specification HD factors TLX1 and TLX3.
source: ASCL1 induces the excitatory neuron specification HD factors TLX1 and TLX3, while PTF1A induces the inhibitory neuron specification HD factor PAX2 (Batista and Lewis, 2008; Borromeo et al., 2014; Chang et al., 2013; Cheng et al., 2004; Cheng et al., 2005; Glasgow et al., 2005; Mizuguchi et al., 2006) (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: PTF1A induces the inhibitory neuron specification HD factor PAX2.
source: ASCL1 induces the excitatory neuron specification HD factors TLX1 and TLX3, while PTF1A induces the inhibitory neuron specification HD factor PAX2 (Batista and Lewis, 2008; Borromeo et al., 2014; Chang et al., 2013; Cheng et al., 2004; Cheng et al., 2005; Glasgow et al., 2005; Mizuguchi et al., 2006) (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: PTF1A increases levels of the transcriptional repressor PRDM13.
source: Since both ASCL1 and PTF1A function as transcriptional activators (Beres et al., 2006; Nakada et al., 2004), the mechanism for repression was discovered to be indirect, involving PTF1A increasing levels of the transcriptional repressor PRDM13 (Chang et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chang et al., 2013.

claim: PRDM13 functions to specify subsets of retinal amacrine interneurons in retina.
source: The role of PRDM13 as a cell type specification factor has been demonstrated in neural tube (Chang et al., 2013) and retina (Watanabe et al., 2015). In retina, PRDM13 functions to specify subsets of retinal amacrine interneurons.
evidence: Supported by citation to Watanabe et al., 2015.

claim: OLIG2 is restricted to the motor neuron progenitor domain (pMN) in the ventral spinal cord at early stages of neurogenesis.
source: OLIG2 is restricted to the motor neuron progenitor domain (pMN) in the ventral spinal cord at these early stages of neurogenesis, and it is required for specification of motor neurons (Mizuguchi et al., 2001; Novitch et al., 2001; Zhou et al., 2000) (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: OLIG2 is required for specification of motor neurons.
source: OLIG2 is restricted to the motor neuron progenitor domain (pMN) in the ventral spinal cord at these early stages of neurogenesis, and it is required for specification of motor neurons (Mizuguchi et al., 2001; Novitch et al., 2001; Zhou et al., 2000) (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: Prdm12 is normally restricted to ventral progenitor domain 1 (p1) and is required for generation of V1 interneurons.
source: Prdm12 is normally restricted to ventral progenitor domain 1 (p1) and is required for generation of V1 interneurons (Thélie et al., 2015) (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by citation to Thélie et al., 2015 and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: PTF1A functions in a trimeric complex with an E-protein and RBPJ.
source: PTF1A functions in a trimeric complex (PTF1) with an E-protein and RBPJ (Meredith et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Meredith et al., 2009.

claim: The 2.3 kb Ptf1a autoregulatory enhancer can direct expression of a GFP reporter gene in the correct domain in transgenic mice and in the chick neural tube.
source: This enhancer can direct expression of a GFP reporter gene in the correct domain in transgenic mice and in the chick neural tube.
evidence: Stated as a known property of the enhancer, supported by previous work.

claim: PTF1A co-electroporation dramatically increases Ptf1a autoregulatory enhancer activity in chick neural tube.
source: As was previously reported, this enhancer directs GFP expression to the Ptf1a domain in the dorsal neural tube and co-electroporation with a Ptf1a expression vector dramatically increases enhancer activity (Figure 5I–J,M).
evidence: Result from chick electroporation reporter assays shown in Figure 5I-J,M.
